newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank opens Lombard access, effective Friday.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank opens Lombard access, effective Friday.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Thursday it would begin allowing banks to access the short-term last resort Lombard lending facility from Friday at a rate of 50 percent.
"We are opening the Lombard credit facility from tomorrow," CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters. "The rate remains the same at 50 percent."
Svehla added that informal limits on non-residents' access to the Czech money market, agreed upon by the CNB and large domestic banks, remained in place.

He said it was the CNB's aim to eventually open the money market again to non-resident investors: "We have the intention, for sure (to remove the informal limits on non-residents), but I cannot specify now when and how we will do this."
The CNB originally limited access, and then closed off the Lombard facility, after a wave of short-selling the crown by speculators pushed the currency to record lows.

Eventually the CNB was forced to allow the crown to float freely, after attempting to prop it up through a series of administrative measures such as the limits and interest rate hikes, and direct market intervention.
"As we move toward a more standard situation we will go gradually down with interest rates," Svehla said.
During the crown crisis, the CNB raised its discount rate to 13 percent from a previous 10.5 percent, and the Lombard rate to 50 percent from 14 percent.

It also hiked its repo rate to 75 percent from 12.9 percent, but has gradually been lowering it to a current level of 31 percent in its one-week operations, and 29 percent in its two-week operations to drain funds from themarket.
